quests.hint: Careful supervision to make sure an industry or process is behaving properly.
quests.explanation: 'Independent oversight' is common in regulation and governance. This word has a second, opposite meaning too — a careless mistake!
quests.textToSpeak: The new law strengthens independent ___ of the financial services industry.
quests.correctAnswer: The new law strengthens independent oversight of the financial services industry.

quests.hint: Official authority or permission, often granted by voters, to carry out a plan.
quests.explanation: 'A clear mandate from voters' is common in politics. As a verb, 'to mandate' means to officially require something.
quests.textToSpeak: The government claimed it had a clear ___ from voters to implement the full reform programme.
quests.correctAnswer: The government claimed it had a clear mandate from voters to implement the full reform programme.

quests.hint: The specific area of responsibility that falls under someone's job or department.
quests.explanation: 'Falls within someone's remit' is common workplace language for describing whose job something actually is.
quests.textToSpeak: Negotiating international treaties falls entirely within the Foreign Office's ___.
quests.correctAnswer: Negotiating international treaties falls entirely within the Foreign Office's remit.

quests.hint: The freedom to make your own decisions without needing constant approval.
quests.explanation: 'Greater autonomy' is a common workplace phrase. The adjective form is 'autonomous' — 'an autonomous team.'
quests.textToSpeak: The proposal would give schools greater ___ to design their own curriculum.
quests.correctAnswer: The proposal would give schools greater autonomy to design their own curriculum.

quests.hint: Openly disagreeing with an official decision, even within your own group.
quests.explanation: 'Record dissent' is formal language for officially noting disagreement. As a verb, 'to dissent' means to hold a different view.
quests.textToSpeak: Three senior ministers recorded their ___ from the cabinet's decision in the official minutes.
quests.correctAnswer: Three senior ministers recorded their dissent from the cabinet's decision in the official minutes.

quests.hint: A formal process where a neutral outsider helps settle a dispute outside of court.
quests.explanation: 'Refer to arbitration' avoids a lengthy court battle. The person who does this is called 'an arbitrator.'
quests.textToSpeak: The employment dispute was referred to independent ___ to avoid a lengthy court battle.
quests.correctAnswer: The employment dispute was referred to independent arbitration to avoid a lengthy court battle.

quests.hint: Something offered to encourage a particular kind of behaviour, often financial.
quests.explanation: 'A financial incentive' is common in HR and business. 'Incentive to' is followed by the base form of a verb.
quests.textToSpeak: The company introduced a new financial ___ to encourage staff to stay long-term.
quests.correctAnswer: The company introduced a new financial incentive to encourage staff to stay long-term.

quests.hint: Influencing someone's opinion, often gently but effectively.
quests.explanation: 'Sway public opinion' is the go-to phrase. As a noun, 'hold sway' means to have significant influence over something.
quests.textToSpeak: A single passionate testimonial can really ___ public opinion.
quests.correctAnswer: A single passionate testimonial can really sway public opinion.

quests.hint: Real influence or power, especially the kind that gets you listened to.
quests.explanation: 'Have clout' is a fairly informal but widely used word for influence, often applied to someone whose opinion genuinely carries weight.
quests.textToSpeak: As the youngest member, she didn't have much ___ in the negotiations at first.
quests.correctAnswer: As the youngest member, she didn't have much clout in the negotiations at first.

quests.hint: The specific numbers used to measure how well something is performing.
quests.explanation: 'Key metrics' is common in marketing and business reporting. The singular form, 'a metric,' refers to just one measurement.
quests.textToSpeak: The company uses several key ___ to measure the success of its marketing campaigns.
quests.correctAnswer: The company uses several key metrics to measure the success of its marketing campaigns.

quests.hint: Deliberately unclear, so it could be interpreted more than one way.
quests.explanation: 'An equivocal response' avoids giving a straight answer. Its opposite is 'unequivocal,' completely clear and certain.
quests.textToSpeak: The minister gave an ___ response that satisfied neither side of the debate.
quests.correctAnswer: The minister gave an equivocal response that satisfied neither side of the debate.

quests.hint: Checking that a fact or claim is actually accurate before relying on it.
quests.explanation: 'Verify every fact' is standard practice in serious journalism. The noun form is 'verification.'
quests.textToSpeak: Before publishing the claim, the editor insisted the team ___ every fact first.
quests.correctAnswer: Before publishing the claim, the editor insisted the team verify every fact first.

quests.hint: Taking action to reduce or cancel out an unwanted effect.
quests.explanation: 'Counteract the effects of' something is the one that sounds most natural. It suggests actively working against a negative force.
quests.textToSpeak: Regular exercise can help ___ the effects of spending all day at a desk.
quests.correctAnswer: Regular exercise can help counteract the effects of spending all day at a desk.

quests.hint: Never-ending, continuing on and on without any real break.
quests.explanation: 'A perpetual state of' something describes an ongoing, seemingly permanent situation. 'Perpetually' is the adverb form.
quests.textToSpeak: The organization has been in a ___ state of crisis since the leadership scandal broke.
quests.correctAnswer: The organization has been in a perpetual state of crisis since the leadership scandal broke.

quests.hint: Extremely old-fashioned and no longer suited to modern life.
quests.explanation: 'Archaic provisions' in law often need updating. It's a stronger, more formal word than simply 'old.'
quests.textToSpeak: Several ___ provisions in the legislation date back over two hundred years and need reform.
quests.correctAnswer: Several archaic provisions in the legislation date back over two hundred years and need reform.

quests.hint: Breaking apart into many smaller, disconnected pieces.
quests.explanation: 'The fragmentation of' a vote or group describes it splitting into competing factions. The verb form is 'fragment.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ of the opposition vote allowed the ruling party to win with a small share.
quests.correctAnswer: The fragmentation of the opposition vote allowed the ruling party to win with a small share.

quests.hint: A strong sense of togetherness that holds a group firmly united.
quests.explanation: 'Community cohesion' is a common phrase in social policy. The adjective form is 'cohesive' — 'a cohesive team.'
quests.textToSpeak: Strong community ___ is essential for managing the social impacts of rapid change.
quests.correctAnswer: Strong community cohesion is essential for managing the social impacts of rapid change.

quests.hint: A structured system with clear levels of rank, from senior to junior.
quests.explanation: 'Flatten the hierarchy' means removing layers of management. The adjective form is 'hierarchical.'
quests.textToSpeak: The company recently flattened its management ___ to speed up decision-making.
quests.correctAnswer: The company recently flattened its management hierarchy to speed up decision-making.

quests.hint: Capturing the whole essence of an idea in just a few words.
quests.explanation: 'Perfectly encapsulate' is high praise for a concise summary. It literally means enclosing something in a small capsule.
quests.textToSpeak: One sentence can sometimes ___ an entire philosophy of life.
quests.correctAnswer: One sentence can sometimes encapsulate an entire philosophy of life.

quests.hint: Drawing out a response or piece of information through skilful questioning.
quests.explanation: 'Elicit a response' is the phrase to remember. Don't confuse it with 'illicit,' which means illegal.
quests.textToSpeak: A good interviewer knows how to ___ honest and detailed answers through careful questioning.
quests.correctAnswer: A good interviewer knows how to elicit honest and detailed answers through careful questioning.

quests.hint: An exclusive right that belongs to someone because of their particular position.
quests.explanation: 'It's entirely her prerogative' means it's her decision alone to make, often used to defend someone's right to choose.
quests.textToSpeak: It is entirely the CEO's ___ to appoint whomever she sees fit for the senior role.
quests.correctAnswer: It is entirely the CEO's prerogative to appoint whomever she sees fit for the senior role.

quests.hint: Currently holding the position, before any election or replacement.
quests.explanation: 'The incumbent prime minister' means the one currently in office. It's also used as an adjective — 'it is incumbent upon you to act.'
quests.textToSpeak: The ___ prime minister was widely expected to lose the election by a significant margin.
quests.correctAnswer: The incumbent prime minister was widely expected to lose the election by a significant margin.

quests.hint: Making a relationship or agreement stronger and more permanent.
quests.explanation: 'Solidify a partnership' is common in business — literally making something solid, no longer liable to change.
quests.textToSpeak: The two companies used the retreat to ___ their new partnership.
quests.correctAnswer: The two companies used the retreat to solidify their new partnership.

quests.hint: Turning informal, unwritten habits into a clear, official set of rules.
quests.explanation: 'Codify conventions into a charter' is common in governance. The noun form is 'codification.'
quests.textToSpeak: The task force was asked to ___ the existing unwritten conventions into a formal charter.
quests.correctAnswer: The task force was asked to codify the existing unwritten conventions into a formal charter.

quests.hint: Severely limiting what someone is able to do.
quests.explanation: 'Constrain the ability to' something is how most speakers say it. The noun form is 'constraint' — 'financial constraints.'
quests.textToSpeak: Limited resources ___ the government's ability to respond quickly to the growing crisis.
quests.correctAnswer: Limited resources constrain the government's ability to respond quickly to the growing crisis.

quests.hint: Arranging a deal or agreement between two sides who wouldn't otherwise cooperate.
quests.explanation: 'Broker a compromise' uses the word as a verb, not just a noun for a financial professional, suggesting skilled negotiation.
quests.textToSpeak: It took a neutral outsider to ___ a compromise between the two founders.
quests.correctAnswer: It took a neutral outsider to broker a compromise between the two founders.

quests.hint: Making it impossible for something to happen, ruling it out completely.
quests.explanation: 'Automatically preclude' is common in formal writing. It's a more precise alternative to simply 'prevent' or 'rule out.'
quests.textToSpeak: His previous conviction did not automatically ___ him from applying for the position.
quests.correctAnswer: His previous conviction did not automatically preclude him from applying for the position.

quests.hint: A complete, thorough rebuild of a system from top to bottom.
quests.explanation: 'Overhaul the filing system' uses the word as a verb. As a noun, 'a major overhaul' describes the same complete rebuild.
quests.textToSpeak: The new manager decided to ___ the entire filing system in her first month.
quests.correctAnswer: The new manager decided to overhaul the entire filing system in her first month.

quests.hint: A small effect that spreads out and impacts things further and further away.
quests.explanation: 'A ripple effect' is a vivid phrase, like the rings spreading out after a stone is dropped in water.
quests.textToSpeak: One late shipment caused a ___ effect that delayed the whole production line.
quests.correctAnswer: One late shipment caused a ripple effect that delayed the whole production line.

quests.hint: Officially putting a new plan or policy into action.
quests.explanation: 'Enact real changes' is common in both government and business. The noun form is 'enactment.'
quests.textToSpeak: The new CEO wasted no time before beginning to ___ real changes across the company.
quests.correctAnswer: The new CEO wasted no time before beginning to enact real changes across the company.
